tracks.note: Content track of an idea or asset (GOAL.md §3.1).

values.label: Remix
values.description: Track A: a reaction to or remix of someone else's clip, made ours by the owner's take and a credit.

values.label: Motion
values.description: Track B: an original 8-bit motion video rendered from a code template.

pillars.note: Placeholders until the channel bible (gate H2, step 049) defines the real pillars. Optional shelf_days per pillar: days after the batch date a submitted video stays worth posting (its default best_before; trend-type short, evergreen long). Without it the BEST_BEFORE_DEFAULT_DAYS setting applies. Optional flags (create_idea guards, src/learning/quotas.py): humour (counts toward HUMOUR_SHARE; every other pillar is informative) and needs_citations (facts: an idea needs at least one citation {url, title?}, GOAL.md §5.6).

values.label: Faits étonnants
values.description: Surprising, checkable facts.

values.label: Idées reçues
values.description: Common beliefs that turn out wrong.

values.label: Histoires
values.description: A short story that explains one idea.

values.label: Humour du quotidien
values.description: Relatable POV moments played for laughs.

hook_types.note: How the first second grabs attention. The agent picks one per idea.

values.label: Question
values.description: Opens with a direct question the viewer wants answered.

values.label: Affirmation forte
values.description: States something surprising or strong as fact, then backs it up.

values.label: Suspense
values.description: Teases an answer or reveal that only comes later in the video.

values.label: POV
values.description: "POV:" sets up a relatable situation the viewer is put into.

values.label: Mythe démonté
values.description: Names a common belief and promises to prove it wrong.

values.label: Liste chiffrée
values.description: Promises a countable list ("3 things...", "5 facts...").

values.label: Histoire
values.description: Drops the viewer into the middle of a short story.

values.label: Défi
values.description: Dares the viewer to guess, answer or beat something before the reveal.

templates.note: Track B (motion) code templates only. Track A assets are described by their recipe, not a template. Ids are PascalCase (component names in motion/).

values.label: Fact Quest
values.description: Hook screen, 3-5 facts as game levels, end card.

values.label: Boss Battle
values.description: A versus B, or myth versus fact, as a boss fight with a verdict.

values.label: Quiz Chest
values.description: Question, choices, countdown, reveal; invites comments.

values.label: Dialog Story
values.description: RPG-style dialogue between the mascot and a character.

values.label: Pixel Skit
values.description: Humour: a 10-20 s relatable POV sketch with a punchline.

values.label: Voxel Quest
values.description: 3D 8-bit (voxel) story in the kitchen set: hook, problem, the app solves it, the golem levels up, animated end card.

values.label: Paper Story
values.description: The owner's house style: paper cut-out story with a named character (Inès, Paul, Sam, Léa): question hook, problem, the app solves it, payoff, paper end card.

values.label: Cutaway
values.description: Pixel explainer (style « Pixel explicatif »): the body as a machine, a cutaway mechanism (muscle, sarcomere, repair, fat cell, mitochondrion) slowed down and labelled by a game HUD; hook question, 4-6 beats, payoff, the HUD's level-complete end card.

values.label: Éditorial
values.description: Black editorial art direction: type-only hook (white grotesk + pink italic serif), 3-5 counted chapters with a pixel blossom tree that grows, cute anatomy characters (stomach, muscle, heart, bone, fat cell) on deep blue cards, before / after split, social-proof numbers, editorial end card.

values.label: Pixel Cinema
values.description: A short film over one living pixel-art set (rainy city at 21 h, dawn run on the pier, the fridge at night): struck-through hook, numbered chips, a lightning frame, a payoff stat or the app card, cinema end card.

values.label: Macro 3D
values.description: Dark photoreal 3D macro explainer (style « Macro 3D »): Blender plates of food and body pieces in a black studio void (rim light, depth of field, slow macro moves, a cut every 1-3 s), word-by-word captions with a blue selection box on the key word, small honest labels, a counter, and Marco the macroBody coach reacting in the corner; 4-10 scenes, tu, Macro 3D end card.

values.label: Sitcom 3D
values.description: Absurd 3D sitcom skit (style « Sitcom 3D »): the Blender troupe (5-8 characters of 16, each in their own colours) in a family dinner, gym, night kitchen, restaurant, living room or beach set, saturated warm light, a cut every 1-2 s with wide, reaction close-ups and top-down angles, x10 fast-forward and slow-mo, the punchline frozen; French voice-over (tu) in bold karaoke captions, characters' short lines in their own voices in speech bubbles, a big number for the key fact, cartoon foley, sitcom end card.

values.label: Physique Scan
values.description: 3D kinetic type on bands (style « Physique Scan », the owner's reference Reel): a detailed muscle cut open, its fibres showing, with 2-6 bands of macro and calorie text that pull tight, rock, whoosh up and down it and squeeze it, a palette per scene (lab, neon, candy); cuts on the bed's beat (orbit, push in, down into the cut, along the muscle), the hook slammed in one word per beat, a measure readout per scene, no voice, physique end card.

feedback_reasons.note: Reason chips in the review inbox (GOAL.md §3.2). Labels are what the chip shows.
